speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly how the swelling in your right knee started and if you have experienced any recent trauma or injury to the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the swelling appear suddenly after minor activities, and have you noticed any excessive bruising or prolonged bleeding from minor cuts? Also, has he had any previous episodes of joint swelling or pain in other areas like elbows or hips?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced any bleeding from the gums, nosebleeds, or prolonged bleeding after vaccinations? I need to assess for other signs of a bleeding disorder given the family history. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ACT: 52.0 s (prolonged), PT: 14.0 s, Thrombin time: < 2 seconds deviation from control

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: The parents report no known allergies, normal birth and developmental history for the child.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, rash, or recent illnesses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must respectfully disagree with that preliminary assessment, as the family history and lack of systemic symptoms strongly point toward a hereditary bleeding disorder like hemophilia rather than tuberculosis. Let's proceed with the coagulation panel to confirm this suspicion.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the coagulation factors are normal, we need to investigate other causes for the joint swelling, such as a bone tumor or infection. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the right knee

text: RESULTS: Ultrasound_Knee: Compatible with hemarthrosis of the right knee, no evidence of fracture or dislocation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms hemarthrosis, which strongly suggests a bleeding disorder despite the initial normal factor VIII and IX levels. I need to rule out von Willebrand disease or Factor XIII deficiency, so REQUEST TEST: Bleeding time and Factor XIII activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the confirmed hemarthrosis, family history, and exclusion of common coagulation factors and von Willebrand disease, I suspect a rare factor deficiency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia C (Factor XI Deficiency)
